{ "sanitize" : false, "textKey" : "", "HTMLTemplateId" : "", "dataJSON" : false, "show" : { "group" : { "operator" : "AND", "rules" : [ { "data" : "ATM unavailable", "condition" : "=", "field" : "ApologiseBranchQueue:TalkTrackApologise:selectedButtonName" } ] } }, "text" : "

Apologise to the customer:

If unhappy that ATM was not working:

 

“I apologise for this. I understand your frustration.”

AND

“I’ll refer this matter to the ATM maintenance team who will investigate it promptly.”

 

If unhappy that an ATM was removed or there are not enough ATMs:

 

“We apologise for the inconvenience.”

AND

“As more customers access digital banking options, we have seen a reduction in the need for cash. This means that ATM use has also declined.

 

“While we’ve removed some ATMs, we can support you to use digital banking options.

 

We also offer ATM services in other locations. The closest ANZ ATM to the ATM you’ve been using is at <insert location>. Does that help you?

 

Also, some other banks offer fee-free ATM withdrawals to ANZ customers using an ANZ card.”

 

Acknowledge concern:

 

“Thank you for raising this with us. I’ve recorded your concerns and will include it in our regular review.”

 

Note: For vulnerable customers, discuss this case with your people leader and refer to Customer Resolution Knowhow page on “Supporting Customers Experiencing Vulnerability”

“I understand your frustration, and I apologise.”

 

OR

 

“I’m sorry about this. I acknowledge that you are dissatisfied with our decisions regarding our branch network.”

AND

“We’ve seen that branch use has decreased significantly, so we have made the difficult decision to close some branches. With more customers banking online, we’re currently focused on making our digital banking experience better.”

 

Acknowledge concern:

 

“Thank you for raising this with us. I’ve recorded your concerns and will include it in our regular review.”

 

(Note: If the customer wants to attend a branch but unable due to

  • remote location (>150km from ANZ branch)
  • disability
  • overseas
  • illness, and/or
  • vulnerability:

discuss this case with your people leader on how best to assist this customer with their needs, and/or refer to “Supporting Customers Experiencing Vulnerability”)

If unhappy with branch facilities or design:

 

“I’m sorry to hear that we haven’t met your expectations about this. It’s important we hear what could be improved or changed.”

OR

“We design our facilities with our customers in mind, and I apologize for not meeting your expectations.

 

If unhappy with trading hours:

 

“I’m sorry we weren’t open at the time you expected us to be.”

OR

“I’m sorry about this, I understand your frustration.”

AND

“We regularly monitor the arrival times of customers and try to cater for all our customers. Our current trading hours are on our website, and you can also make an appointment.

 

As more of our customers are choosing to use digital banking options instead of visiting the branch, our branch trading hours may reflect that. We’re also investing in making our digital banking experience better.”

 

Acknowledge concern:

 

“Thank you for raising this with us. I’ve recorded your concerns and this will be considered as part of our internal review.”

 

Note: For vulnerable customers, discuss this case with your people leader and refer to Customer Resolution Knowhow page on “Supporting Customers Experiencing Vulnerability”

childElements.propertySetConfig:
{ "controlWidth" : 12, "label" : "TextBlock1", "text" : "

Provide information to the customer:

 

If the customer has confirmed their issue is about branch queue/wait time, ask the customer:

 

“Would you like me to tell you about how you can do more of your banking online?”

 

  • If yes - go to “Ways to bank” page on the ANZ website, and guide the customer through the different ways they can manage their money besides going to the branch.
  • If no – continue below

 

“We do have branches that offer full branch services if you need that. Would you like me to tell you how to find these?”

 

(If customer says yes):

 

“You can visit “locations” on our website, look for “full branch services” listed under their Services section.  You can also book an appointment from the website.”

 

 

Check for additional issues:

 

“Were there any other issues you wanted to raise?”

 

By clicking Next, you will be directed back to the Choose Pathway page to Consider Additional Issues.

childElements.propertySetConfig:
{ "sanitize" : false, "textKey" : "", "HTMLTemplateId" : "", "dataJSON" : false, "show" : { "group" : { "operator" : "AND", "rules" : [ { "data" : "Unable to continue call", "condition" : "=", "field" : "ProvideinformationBranchQueue:TalkTrackProvideInfo:selectedButtonName" } ] } }, "text" : "

If customer wants to continue phone conversation at another time:

 

“I’m happy to continue this discussion at a more convenient time. When might be best for you?”

 

(agree on a time with customer for you to call them back)

 

“I will speak to you again <repeat time and date agreed>. Thank you for your time.”

 

(END CALL)

 

If customer

  • doesn’t want to continue phone conversation at another time, AND/OR
  • prefers a written response

 

“I’ll send you my written response to your complaint. Thank you for raising this matter with us.”

 

(END CALL)

 

If customer

  • does not wish to discuss the complaint at all, AND
  • says they don’t want a written response either:

 

“ANZ has an obligation to give you a written response. However, if you don’t want this, we can withdraw your complaint. Would you like me to do that on your behalf?”

 

(If customer says yes – withdraw complaint)

(If customer says no – explain to customer):

 

“As you don’t want to withdraw the complaint, we are required to send you a written response. This will include AFCA’s details so you can escalate further if you wish.”

 

(END CALL)
